# AI Topic dialogue synthesis
# Aliases: rivet='Rivet', patch='Patch'

# Predicted ~83s (1082 chars) targeting 90s

Rivet: Stop touching the printer.

Patch: That is a very dramatic way to begin a lesson.

Rivet: You called me over because the print behaved strangely, then changed the settings, moved the model, and started another print before I arrived.

Patch: I was narrowing it down.

Rivet: You were broadening it enthusiastically. Here is the lesson: first say what happened. Not what you think happened. What happened.

Patch: Fine. The first print did not come out the way I expected.

Rivet: Good. That is an observation. “The printer dislikes me personally” is an explanation, and not presently a useful one.

Patch: It has seen what I ask of it. The case is not weak.

Rivet: Then we run the same thing again before we declare a cause. If it happens once, it is interesting. If it happens again under the same conditions, we have something to investigate. And this time, change one thing at a time.

Patch: That feels slower than my usual process.

Rivet: Your usual process is how we end up with six possible explanations and a printer wearing tape like a hat.

Patch: All right. Same model. Same settings. I touch nothing.

Rivet: Excellent. Now we may begin the experiment you were already having.
